faqs.question: Can I leave Mumbai airport during a layover?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you can enter India and you have enough time. Leaving means clearing immigration, so you need a valid Indian visa or e-Visa unless you are an Indian citizen or OCI cardholder. Then allow for the drive each way and around 3 hours back at the airport before an international departure.

faqs.question: How long a layover do I need to leave the airport?
faqs.answer: As a rough rule, at least 6 hours on the ground, and ideally 8 or more. With 6 hours and carry-on bags only, a short outing near the airport can work if your inbound flight lands on time. With 8 hours, South Mumbai comes within reach.

faqs.question: Do I need a visa if I stay inside the airport?
faqs.answer: If you connect from one international flight to another inside the international transit area, without passing through passport control, you don’t need an Indian visa. You just can’t leave the airport.

faqs.question: What if my inbound flight lands late?
faqs.answer: Run the numbers again with the new landing time. If the window drops below what a place needs, stay airside. Detour routes are built backwards from your departure, so stops get trimmed, never the time you need for your flight.

faqs.question: What do I do with my bags?
faqs.answer: If your bags are checked through to your final destination, you don’t need to touch them. If you have to collect them, the airport has a left-luggage cloakroom; allow a few extra minutes at each end.
